Olivia (Product): Heads-up: customer X and Y escalated asks for the Optimize toolkit — they want deterministic per-request cost guidance + eval-triggered alerts tied to prompt sets. Need to decide Q3 pilot scope and clear launch criteria.
Rory (Eng): Do we have usage signals from pilot accounts to justify prioritization?
Maya (Data): Shared a quick heatmap: https://redwood.internal/heatmaps/pilot-usage (summary: short-chat flows = ~70% of calls p50 tokens, long generative jobs ~20%). Batching yields biggest wins on long jobs; prefix caching helps short repeated prompts. Recommend pilot focus on adaptive batching + KV prefix cache + basic alerting.
Sean (ML): Customer Z also asked about quantization (8-bit) with eval hooks. Risk: small quality regressions on open-domain prompts. We should require eval gating and canary fallback if we touch quant.
Olivia (Product): Proposed customer-impact matrix: rank by user pain (revenue impact, SLO hits) vs dev cost. My pilot MVP suggestion: (1) adaptive batching policies, (2) prefix cache with TTL and per-tenant controls, (3) eval-triggered alert wiring (signal taxonomy). Quantization = stretch.
Rory (Eng): Agree. Operational risk for aggressive quantization is non-trivial. If we include it, need canary + automatic fallback routing to fp16 variants. That adds infra work.
Maya (Data): For eval-triggered alerts we need: standard prompt-sets per customer, baseline metrics, and drift detectors. Candidate signals: token distribution shift, perplexity delta, and embedding-similarity drop against golden answers.
Amanda (Sales): Customers will consider quantization if we commit to a measurable SLA: e.g., "no >1% quality regression on key prompts". They care about percent cost savings too.
Olivia (Product): Can we agree on numerical launch criteria for pilot GA? My draft: - <=1% regression on NPS prompt set (automated + sample human checks) - >=15% token cost reduction for 3 pilot tenants over 30 days - p95 latency within existing SLO for interactive tiers.
Sean (ML): Need to specify regression measurement: propose pairwise embedding-sim + BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, and human review for >threshold failures (sample size 50 per tenant). Define thresholds in the test harness.
Rory (Eng): Rough effort estimates: batching + cache = ~3 sprints (eng + infra); eval-alerting infra + taxonomy = ~2 sprints (data + infra); quantization safety + gating = ~4 sprints (research + eng + ops).
Olivia (Product): Tradeoff proposal: ship batching + cache + eval-alerts in Q3 pilot, keep quantization as Q4 stretch unless a customer offers funding or it's trivial. Thoughts?
Amanda (Sales): :thumbsup: I can push customers for pilot funding and surface which ones would sign up for a quant beta.
Chris (Eng-SRE): Ops items: we need RBAC for tenant-uploaded prompt sets, retention/TTL policy for cached prefixes, and per-tenant throttles for the caching layer. Also add rollout playbook for fallback routing.
Olivia (Product): Action items: @Rory prototype an adaptive batching config and share perf sims by EOD next Mon (example config snippet below). @Maya finalize signal taxonomy for eval-alerts and hand off detector recipes. @Sean draft quant gating & canary playbook. I'll prepare the customer-impact matrix doc for leadership review.
Rory (Eng): Example batching config:
```
batch.window_ms = 10
batch.max_tokens = 2048
policy = "latency-first"  # or "cost-first"
```
Maya (Data): I'll post the signal taxonomy doc and a quick notebook with detection thresholds.
Sean (ML): I'll outline the gating criteria: unit tests -> eval-run -> canary with 5% traffic -> 24h quality check window -> auto-rollback.
Olivia (Product): Thanks all — will sync this into the roadmap doc and propose the Q3 pilot slice: batching + cache + eval-alerts, quantization as funded stretch.
